version_pins.quote: The finest token boundary (in tokens) a prefix-cache hit can land on. Prefix-cache keys are computed every `prefix_match_unit` tokens. It can be set finer than the physical KV cache block sizes (e.g. 32 vs a 1024-token hybrid-model block) as long as every KV cache group's `block_size` is divisible by it, enabling cache hits at boundaries inside a physical block. It controls matching granularity only, not how often states are stored. This equals to the `hash_block_size` used throughout the KV cache code.

state_snapshot_grid.quote: With prefix caching enabled, Mamba state is stored only on the Mamba block grid, so a prefix-cache hit can resume only at a block boundary. `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` also stores a checkpoint at the shared-prefix junction, the point where an earlier request with the same prefix stopped. Requests whose shared prefix ends inside a block can then reuse it.
state_snapshot_grid.reading: block grid = the resolved block size (1088 / 1056 / 2096 in our cells), NOT --block-size as passed

why_unset_prefix_match_unit_floors_every.quote:
requested = cache_config.prefix_match_unit
    hash_block_size = (
        requested if requested is not None else math.gcd(*group_block_sizes)
    )
    if any(bs % hash_block_size != 0 for bs in group_block_sizes):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid prefix_match_unit={hash_block_size}; all KV cache group "
            f"block sizes must be divisible by prefix_match_unit. "
            f"Got group block sizes={group_block_sizes}."
        )
    return scheduler_block_size, hash_block_size
why_unset_prefix_match_unit_floors_every.reading: for a hybrid model the mamba group block_size is forced equal to the attention block (platforms/interface.py:900 / :918), so GCD = block size. Hash keys therefore exist only on the big block grid and every hit rounds down to it - which is exactly the measured reuse law cached = block*floor(L/block).

partial_tail_registration_is_disabled_by.reading: prompt-tail caching at hash granularity exists in 0.27.1 but is dead code while prefix_match_unit is unset (hash_block_size == block_size). Setting --prefix-match-unit re-enables it for BOTH the attention group and the mamba 'align' group (MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block, :1683-1730).

can_prefix_match_unit_go_below_block.answer: yes, explicitly supported, with a divisibility contract
can_prefix_match_unit_go_below_block.quote: It can be set finer than the physical KV cache block sizes (e.g. 32 vs a 1024-token hybrid-model block) as long as every KV cache group's `block_size` is divisible by it, enabling cache hits at boundaries inside a physical block. It controls matching granularity only, not how often states are stored.
can_prefix_match_unit_go_below_block.caveat: the last sentence is the catch: finer keys do not create finer state snapshots. A mamba group can only hit at a boundary that actually has a registered state (dense block grid, or the registered prompt tail). So the win is on turn tails, not on arbitrary interior boundaries - closure of that gap is exactly what v0.30.1's --enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint adds.

native_tier_wiring.reading: --kv-offloading-size N is sugar: it builds a KVTransferConfig whose connector is OffloadingConnector (or SimpleCPUOffloadConnector when VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD is set) with cpu_bytes_to_use = N GiB. The same tier is reachable explicitly via --kv-transfer-config {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector",...,"cpu_bytes_to_use":...}.

documented_sizing_rule.quote: For single-tier (CPU-only) setups, set `cpu_bytes_to_use` larger than the aggregate GPU KV cache. Because offloading is immediate, a smaller CPU tier just mirrors what the GPU already holds and adds no hit rate.
documented_sizing_rule.reading: sizing rule is: CPU tier must exceed aggregate GPU KV capacity, otherwise no extra hit rate. Also 'cpu_bytes_to_use ... Total bytes of host memory reserved for the CPU tier across all workers (not per-worker).'

mamba_is_supported_by_the_offload_tier.quote: For MambaSpec groups in "align" cache mode the hit window must be rounded
mamba_is_supported_by_the_offload_tier.reading: resolve_mamba_align_size() exists, so the native offload connector does handle mamba 'align' groups; but the kv_offloading_usage.md events note says 'Full-attention groups only; sliding-window/SSM groups keep the placeholder fallback' for self-describing events - i.e. telemetry for SSM blocks is degraded even where offload works. Disk/secondary tiers exist only in the TieringOffloadingSpec path (fs/obj/p2p secondary_tiers), not as a --kv-offloading-size sub-flag.

phase_quotes: # Phase 1: Pick block size from backend (skip if user set --block-size)

# Phase 2: Align block/mamba sizes for hybrid models
        # (may override user settings).

# Phase 3: Align block/page sizes when multiple KV dtypes share the
        # block pool (e.g. nvfp4 primary + unquantized skip layers).
        # May override the user's --block-size.
code_path.resolution_quote:
if cache_config.mamba_cache_mode == "all":
            # With prefix caching, align to mamba chunk size for kernel perf
            ...
            base_chunk_size = mamba_block_size or model_config.get_mamba_chunk_size()
            attn_tokens_per_mamba_state = cdiv(mamba_page_size, attn_page_size_1_token)
            chunk_size = lcm(base_chunk_size, kernel_block_alignment_size)
            attn_block_size = chunk_size * cdiv(attn_tokens_per_mamba_state, chunk_size)
            cache_config.mamba_block_size = attn_block_size
        else:
            ...
            attn_block_size = kernel_block_alignment_size * cdiv(
                mamba_page_size,
                kernel_block_alignment_size * attn_page_size_1_token,
            )

        if cache_config.block_size < attn_block_size:
            cache_config.block_size = attn_block_size
code_path.how_user_block_size_enters: only through kernel_block_alignment_size = max(min(backend supported kernel block size), cache_config.block_size) (interface.py:874-884), which then feeds lcm() and the rounding-up cdiv(). So a larger --block-size can only raise the resolved value, never lower it, and the final number is always a multiple of chunk_size derived from the Mamba page size.
code_path.consistent_with_our_evidence: resolved 1088 (user 64) > resolved 1056 (user 16) is exactly the predicted direction: the 64 case floors kernel_block_alignment_size to 64, the 16 case to the backend's smallest supported kernel block (32), and lcm(base_chunk, align) then yields a larger chunk for 1088 than 1056. The default cell (2096) is the same formula with Phase 1's backend-preferred block plus Phase 3's nvfp4 heterogeneous-KV bump.
code_path.cannot_pin_exact_constants: 1088 / 1056 / 2096 cannot be reconstructed from public source alone: attn_tokens_per_mamba_state = cdiv(mamba_page_size, attn_page_size_1_token) needs the model's get_mamba_state_shape_from_config shapes/dtypes and get_mamba_chunk_size (vllm/config/model.py:1531), i.e. the served checkpoint's head layout and linear-attention state width. Verify by reading the startup log lines rather than by formula.

chain_hash.quote:
Block 2: |<------- prefix ------>| |<--- block tokens --->|
...Therefore, we can build the block hash of `hash(tuple[components])`, where components are:

* Parent hash value: The hash value of the parent hash block.
* Block tokens: A tuple of tokens in this block.
* Extra hashes: Other values required to make this block unique, such as LoRA IDs, multi-modality input hashes (see the example below), and cache salts to isolate caches in multi-tenant environments.
chain_hash.reading: strictly chained prefix: any token change at or before block k changes the hash of block k and therefore of every block after it. There is no suffix/delta cache. Mid-context insertion invalidates the tail from the insertion point onward regardless of --prefix-match-unit.

full_blocks_only.quote:
!!! note "Note 1"
    We only cache full blocks.
full_blocks_only.reading: at hash granularity 'full block' means full hash unit; that is why --prefix-match-unit is the only knob that moves the granularity of that sentence

cache_salt.quote: By including a `cache_salt` in the request, this value is injected into the hash of the first block, ensuring that only requests with the same salt can reuse cached KV blocks.
cache_salt.reading: whole-prefix isolation, not suffix pinning; use only if you need tenant isolation

options.our_value: unset (None) in every measured cell -> hash_block_size = GCD(group block sizes) = resolved block size (1088 / 1056 / 2096)
options.recommended: 16 (or 32 only where every group block size is divisible by 32: valid for 1088 and 1056, INVALID for 2096 because 2096 % 32 = 16)
options.why: This is the only knob in 0.27.1 that moves the reuse boundary off the block grid. Unset, vLLM hashes only at block granularity and _cache_partial_tail_block is skipped (block_size == hash_block_size), so a 71-turn schedule loses every turn that ends mid-block - which reproduces our cached = block*floor(L/block) law exactly. Set to 16, hashes exist every 16 tokens and the prompt-tail partial registration re-activates for both the attention and mamba 'align' groups, so the next turn can resume at 16-token granularity instead of the block floor.
options.quote: It can be set finer than the physical KV cache block sizes (e.g. 32 vs a 1024-token hybrid-model block) as long as every KV cache group's `block_size` is divisible by it, enabling cache hits at boundaries inside a physical block. It controls matching granularity only, not how often states are stored.
options.expected_effect: measured hit fraction should move from floor-to-block (0.9012) toward floor-to-16 behaviour; the size of the gain is exactly the fraction of turns whose prompt length did not end on a block multiple. Startup risk: a wrong value raises ValueError naming the offending sizes (kv_cache_utils.py:682-687), so this fails loud, never silently. Estimate: if turn ends are uniformly distributed over a 2096-token block, floor-to-16 recovers ~99% of the block-rounding loss; this is the single highest-expected-value flag for the 0.9012 vs 0.9572 gap.

options.flag: --enable-prefix-caching (must be explicit) + read the resolved mamba mode from the log
options.our_value: not recorded in this lane's evidence - our 0.9012 hit fraction implies caching was active, but the flag line was not captured
options.recommended: pass --enable-prefix-caching explicitly and capture the startup log lines 'Mamba cache mode is set to ... by default when prefix caching is enabled' and 'Setting attention block size to N tokens ...'
options.why: For hybrid models prefix caching is opt-in in 0.27.1, and the mamba state mode ('all' if the model class advertises supports_mamba_prefix_caching, else 'align') is chosen for you. 'align' stores state only at the last token of a scheduler step at i*block_size, so it is the mode where the block floor bites hardest; 'all' snapshots every block boundary. You cannot reason about capacity or hit rate until you know which branch ran.
options.expected_effect: removes the largest silent-configuration risk in the whole comparison: an 'align' cell and an 'all' cell are not the same experiment, and the opt-in default means an un-flagged launch caches nothing at all.

options.our_value: None in every cell (no offload tier at all)
options.recommended: set it to comfortably more than the aggregate GPU KV cache, e.g. headroom x that figure, host RAM permitting; keep backend native for the in-process tier, and only reach for lmcache/TieringOffloadingSpec if you need a disk tier
options.why: This is the capacity lever: it is the only documented way to hold more reusable prefix than the GPU pool, and the documented sizing rule says a smaller-than-GPU CPU tier adds no hit rate because offload is immediate. A 71-turn schedule's early turns are exactly what eviction costs us.
options.quote: For single-tier (CPU-only) setups, set `cpu_bytes_to_use` larger than the aggregate GPU KV cache. Because offloading is immediate, a smaller CPU tier just mirrors what the GPU already holds and adds no hit rate.
options.expected_effect: raises the ceiling on how much of a 32k-token, 71-turn prefix survives across turns; hit fraction becomes capacity-bound instead of eviction-bound. Semantics: GiB, summed across TP ranks (not per rank); activates only when non-None; forwards to cpu_bytes_to_use = N GiB on the OffloadingConnector.

Current docs state the limitation plainly, which is the strongest available confirmation that our block-floor observation is a known-and-addressed design property rather than a misconfiguration.

Requests whose shared prefix ends inside a block can then reuse it.

NOTE the MTP tension for us: our serving needed --speculative-config mtp REMOVED, so the flag's own precondition ('EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding on the Mamba group') is NOT met on our box - treat this as roadmap, not a switch.

In newer releases the flag is deprecated entirely (no effect, removal in v0.33.0), so it is a bad axis to build an experiment on.

top3: 1. --prefix-match-unit 16 (NOT 32 if the default 2096 block is in play: 2096 % 32 = 16) - the only 0.27.1 knob that moves the reuse boundary off the block grid; unset it and _cache_partial_tail_block is dead code, which is precisely why we observe cached = block*floor(L/block).

2. --enable-prefix-caching explicitly + capture the auto-derived mamba cache mode ('all' vs 'align') and the 'Setting attention block size to N tokens' log line - hybrid prefix caching is opt-in in 0.27.1 and the two modes are different experiments.

3. --kv-offloading-size (GiB, summed over TP ranks) with native backend, sized ABOVE the aggregate GPU KV cache per the documented rule - the only documented capacity tier, and a smaller tier provably adds no hit rate.
unresolved: Exact provenance of 1088 / 1056 / 2096 is formula-level explained (interface.py:890-915) but not reproducible numerically from public source: attn_tokens_per_mamba_state needs the checkpoint's mamba state shape and get_mamba_chunk_size. Resolve by capturing the startup log ('Setting attention block size to %d tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size') and the 'Padding mamba page size by %.2f%%' line per cell.

Which of 'all' / 'align' ran in each of our cells is not in this lane's evidence; the two modes differ in both snapshot density and hit semantics, so any cross-engine number without this pinned is not a controlled comparison.

Whether nvfp4 KV dtype (Phase 3, _align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size, interface.py:647-780) fired in our cells: it can raise block size a second time and it also sets skip_page_size_padded/mamba_page_size_padded, which would change the mamba page geometry. Needs --kv-cache-dtype from the actual launch line plus the 'Setting attention block size to %d tokens so the quantized primary KV page covers the higher-precision padded-spec page.' log.

No documented suffix-pinning / mid-context-insertion feature exists in vLLM at v0.27.1 or in current docs; invalidation is a hard chained-prefix property. If a paper claim needs 'suffix reuse', vLLM cannot support it and the claim must be scoped to SGLang/other engine or dropped.

kv_offloading_size is undocumented in docs/** at v0.27.1 (only --kv-transfer-config OffloadingConnector is documented); the 'larger than aggregate GPU KV' rule is stated for cpu_bytes_to_use. Treat the mapping as source-verified (config/vllm.py:909-917) but doc-silent, and note the events limitation: 'Full-attention groups only; sliding-window/SSM groups keep the placeholder fallback.'

Interaction between --num-gpu-blocks-override and hybrid group-aware capacity is unverified: CacheConfig.kv_cache_size_tokens is documented as 'group-aware capacity since num_gpu_blocks * block_size can be wrong for hybrid models', so any tokens-per-block arithmetic done from num_gpu_blocks alone (as our earlier notes may have) is wrong for this model family.
parent_note: Answers to the four questions: (1) flag existence table above - --enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint does NOT exist in 0.27.1 (landed v0.30.1) and --swap-space is removed from V1; everything else on the list exists. (2) prefix_match_unit may go below block if it divides every group block size; the single best capacity lever is --kv-offloading-size sized above aggregate GPU KV; the single best hit-rate lever is --prefix-match-unit. (3) prefix cache is strictly chained-prefix, full hash units only, no suffix pinning anywhere. (4) --block-size is only a floor: Phase 2 _align_hybrid_block_size overrides it via lcm(mamba chunk, kernel alignment) rounded up to cover the mamba page size, and Phase 3 can raise it again for nvfp4 KV.
